Cost: 1,000eb (Very Expensive) ♦ Install: Clinic

Humanity Loss: 7 (2d6)

In 2073, an actor got an implant designed to enable incredible martial arts speed, primarily so they looked better on camera. When these hands were first activated, the extra on the other end of the barrage was beaten to a bloody and dead pulp. Dynalar thus extracted the studio techie responsible, and two weeks later released a mass-market version.

Paired Cyberhands. Requires Paired Cyberarms and 2 Cyberarm Option Slots on each Cyberarm. These must be installed together and count as a single item for the purposes of Cost and Humanity Loss but not Critical Injuries or Repair. When the user is about to make their first Brawling or Martial Arts attack in a Round not done during a Grapple, they may choose to instead attempt a Blazing Fury Attack.

When making a Blazing Fury Attack, the user makes a single Brawling or Martial Arts Check at a -4 penalty against the target’s Evasion. If they succeed, they roll their usual Brawling or Martial Arts damage, which is then reduced by half (Round Up) and then multiplied by the amount they beat the target’s Evasion Check by, up to a maximum equal to half their level (Round Up) in the requisite skill.

If the user misses their Blazing Fury attack, they must spend an Action on their next turn to recover from the wild flailing before they can make any other Action. Blazing Fury Attacks count as hitting a target with two Brawling or Martial Arts Attacks for the purposes of Martial Arts Special Moves prerequisites.

Type: Cyberarm
Install: Clinic
Option Slots: uses 2

Foundry notes:

  • One item for the pair, as Corgo prices and installs them together. Its size is the 2 slots it takes in one arm; it needs 2 in each.
  • The Blazing Fury damage multiplier is rolled by hand.

From Corgo's 77 Collection V3 by Corgopolis (Cyberware > Cyberarms).
